speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: For example, those who have retired with private savings, and those who are receiving financial support from economically active family members.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: We do not have further details of the financial situation of the 164,000 citizens, as we only collect information required for tax administration.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I think we can do a little bit more for those who have no income rather than no taxable income.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: At the end of the day, at each Budget, we see benefits like the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Vouchers being given to those who stay in Housing and Development Board flats who have income.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: But for those who are in private property, they do not reap the benefits.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: They do not even get the benefit of things like digital television starter kits and they definitely do not qualify for service and conservancy charges rebates.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I am just wondering whether the Government would want to review the policy to try to identify citizens who generally do not have income staying in private property and who would reap benefits of some of these Budget provisions for them.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Indeed, the Government's concern is the same as the Member's, which is, to make sure that all Singaporeans who are in need are taken care of.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, I think there are a few things.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: One, we have broad-based schemes and, for broad-based schemes, you need to have fairly rough and ready proxy indicators.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And out of those, some actually may have financial resources, either because of savings or they may have non-taxable income by way of dividends or interest, or their children may be looking after them.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The challenge then becomes, out of that 164,000, how do you identify the ones who really may have no income at all and may need some assistance.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The way it is designed is for those to do so by application.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And we do have broad-based schemes like the Pioneer Generation Package that applies to all, even those in private properties, and the upcoming Merdeka Generation Package.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, the ones who do not benefit from the broad-based schemes, we would encourage them to apply if in genuine need because the system does allow for appeals and consideration of particular circumstances.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: I do have residents who stay in private property.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: But when they look at the Budget provisions and they see that they get nothing, whereas those who stay in 5-room flats, who earn more than them get the benefits of the Budget provisions.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: They, too, have done their part for the nation.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: They are disadvantaged purely because they live in a private property.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: So, they ask where is the equity of it all because, at the end of the day, they earn less than certain groups of people who earn more but living in 4- or 5-room flats.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: This group of people may be younger, earn more, and they get more from the Budget compared to them who are retired, living on interest income or dividend income.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: I would not say that they are poor.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: But they feel that, "I, too, have done my part in building this country up".

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Can the Government not consider what they have contributed and give them more in terms of providing for them in the Budget?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We shall try to see what we can do to dislodge that!

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In the meantime, if I may address the specific question the Member has raised.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I can understand how some of his residents may feel.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It may be too much of a generalisation, though, to say that there is nothing for them at all in the Budget.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because, for example, education is broad-based and it applies to even those who are in private property.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, for polyclinics and other healthcare services, these are also available to them.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And not forgetting things like last year's SG Bonus.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That would have gone to everybody, irrespective of the property that they were living in.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is important to look at the specific social scheme.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is the reason why it is structured such that you look at their income and you look at the type of property that they stay in.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We will address those on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In terms of recognition, it should not be forgotten that things like the Pioneer Generation Package and the Merdeka Generation Package were specifically designed to give recognition.
